Executive summary
The United Nations Country Team in Uruguay, composed of the WB, ECLAC, FAO, IMF, ILO/CINTERFOR, PHO/WHO, UNIDO, UNDP, UNESCO, UNFPA and UNICEF, worked together between 2005 and 2006 in the preparation of the United Nations Development Assistance Framework (UNDAF) for Uruguay, for the period 2007/2010. This process was characterized by the permanent joint action of the various agencies involved and was nurtured by the results of consultation with government representatives, the civil society (in particular with NGOs), the private sector, the educational establishment and from international cooperation within the country.
The areas of assistance are as follows:
Assistance Area 1: Sustained and sustainable growth of the Uruguayan economy, with emphasis on the diversification of production, insertion in international markets (both within and outside the region), increased incorporation of scientific and technological innovation in productive processes and the growth of investment.
UNDAF Outcome 1: By 2010 the country will have made progress in the generation of the capacity to incorporate knowledge, innovation and diversification in the production of goods and services aimed at sustained and sustainable growth.
Assistance Area 2: To reduce the significant levels of poverty which Uruguayan society has reached in recent years (in particular amongst the younger generations), with emphasis on the eradication of extreme poverty and the reduction of inequities (economic, social, inter-generational, gender, territorial and ethnic) in starting conditions and access to quality social services. 
UNDAF Outcome 2.1.
By 2010, the country will have advanced in the design and management of policies to eradicate indigence and reduce poverty. 
UNDAF Outcome 2.2.
By 2010, the country will have advanced in the design and management of policies which will make possible more equitable starting conditions and increased access to good social services as well as confronting discrimination and promoting processes of social integration. 
Assistance Area 3:
To promote the exercise of all Human Rights and strengthen the quality of democracy, by increasing civil, political and social awareness.
UNDAF Outcome 3: By 2010, the country will have advanced in the adjustment of national legislation and practices to its international commitments, and in the strengthening of public and civil institutions for the design, execution, monitoring and evaluation of public policies.
The resources programmed by the United Nations System in the country, in the areas of cooperation which have been referred to here, are estimated to amount to US$ 32,819,000 for the period 2007-2010. This amount includes the programme resources corresponding to the agencies, funds or programmes themselves (US$ 7,378,000), but excludes salaries and expenses related to the administration of the United Nations offices. It also includes non-refundable bilateral or multilateral or decentralized cooperation (U$S 25,438,000) and excludes repayable loans. 
It should be pointed out that the proposed values arise from projections made by the various agencies and are based on their present use of resources. Also, the period that is covered exceeds the scope of existing programmes (see section “Estimate of Resources Required”). Furthermore, although the document proposes areas of intervention, the execution of such intervention will depend on the financing which is obtained, which in the case of the Specialized Agencies cannot be known for certain at the time of signing this document.  
The assistance areas reflect the joint efforts of the agencies, funds and programmes of the United Nations System which took part in preparing the UNDAF, and do not presume to reflect all global, regional and sub-regional resources, nor the direct contributions made by the offices of the agencies which form part of the United Nations System in Uruguay. 
The United Nations Country Team considers the UNDAF 2007-2010 to be an approach to joint planning and regards it as a flexible framework which can be adapted to changes in national priorities. Furthermore, it is flexible insofar as all of its components can be perfected and modified in order to ensure maximum effectiveness in assisting the country’s development.
Country Team Letter
With the purpose of confronting the challenge posed by the country’s development, the Agencies of the United Nations System in Uruguay initiated a process of joint reflection, shared tasks, support and close cooperation with the Uruguayan Government, in order to outline a vision of the country and help in the preparation of an agenda to support the achievement of equity, human rights, development, peace and security, and which may improve living conditions and the welfare of all Uruguayans. 
	The outcome of this effort was the United Nations System Development Assistance Framework (UNDAF) for Uruguay 2007-2010, which establishes the assistance areas and the results which it is hoped will be achieved. These wide areas of assistance are determined by long-term national priorities and by the comparative advantages of the intervention of the United Nations System in Uruguay. The Country Team believes this document to be of the utmost importance as a framework to improve the effectiveness of development aid. Furthermore, it considers it to be crucial as a guide for the efforts supporting the country in its progress towards development with equity, which will encourage the advance towards the achievement of the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) and other commitments undertaken within the framework of the United Nations.

Assistance Area 2:

UNDAF Outcome 2.1.
By 2010, the country will have advanced in the design and management of policies to eradicate indigence and reduce poverty. 
UNDAF Outcome 2.2.

The United Nations Development Assistance Framework in Uruguay, for the period 2007-2010, was formally presented to the authorities of the Government of Uruguay on 28 April 2006, at the Presidency of the Republic of Uruguay – Budget and Planning Department (acronym in Spanish: OPP).
(Signatures: 
Director of the Budget and Planning Department,
Resident Coordinator of the United Nations in Uruguay)
Montevideo, 28 April 2006
I.   Introduction
The United Nations Development Assistance Framework (UNDAF) is an essential element in the organization reform process begun by the Secretary General. Its principal aim is to improve the effectiveness of United Nations System interventions in countries. UNDAF Uruguay 2007-2010 seeks to maximize the effectiveness of the United Nations in development assistance, providing the Government of Uruguay, the civil society, the cooperating community and other counterparts with backing and support, according to the guidelines set forth by the international community .
The areas selected for aid are in keeping with national priorities and the Millennium Development Goals. In this sense, the document makes use of the contributions, exchanges and conclusions gathered during the debates which took place during the “Negotiating Table” process regarding the Millennium Development Goals, between October 2003 and April 2004. It also makes use of the process reports and the country report summary presented by the government of Uruguay at the United Nations on March 10, 2005, after an extensive process of consultation in which over 2,000 people from different parts of the country took part. This process was favourably mentioned by “Social Watch”, an organization responsible for worldwide MDG monitoring. Furthermore, the UNDAF was drawn up in 2005 and early 2006; the details of this process are included in the appropriate section.
The United Nations Country Team considers that these documents contain long-term priorities. The assistance areas and direct results proposed in the Common Country Assessment (CCA) were endorsed by the government of Uruguay in November 2005 and February 2006. 
In the UNDAF prioritization workshop held with the support of colleagues from the United Nations Staff College on November 15 and 16, 2005, the three assistance areas for the development of Uruguay were established on the basis of national priorities, strengths and comparative advantages of the United Nations System in the country. 
On March 8, 2006, a first draft of the document was sent to the external readers group and on March 13, 2006, the United Nations System Resident Coordinator in Uruguay personally delivered it to the Director of Uruguay’s Budget and Planning Department (abbreviation in Spanish: OPP). Comments and suggestions from both were received on April 11 and 20, 2006, respectively, and were incorporated into the final document. 
The last meeting of the Country Team was held on April 26, 2006 and the final version of the document was endorsed on April 28, 2006. 
In order to determine the UNDAF overall areas of assistance, the United Nations Country Team based itself on the analysis of the following variables:
Characterization of Uruguay by the United Nations Country Team.
National priorities determined in the light of the main documents drawn up by the government.
Competitive advantages of the United Nations System’s intervention in the country. 
The United Nations Country Team discussed the economic, political, social and cultural elements which define Uruguay, on the basis of the CCA, the National Report on MDGs, and other documents for analysis and national evolution produced by the various United Nations System programmes, funds and agencies. 
The Process of drawing up the UNDAF
The implementation of the United Nations reform, regarding the harmonized programming of agencies in Uruguay began with the preparation of the CCA/UNDAF in early 2005, simultaneously with the assumption of the new national government in March of that year. This synchronization made it possible for the United Nations System to work on the basis of the national priorities set forth by the government at the beginning of its term of office, embodied in the strategic direction of the national budget and announced at the Ministers’ Council of August 3, 2005. 
In the middle of the first half of the year, a CCA workshop was held, which included government officials and officials from the United Nations System in the country. The result of this workshop was the achievement of consensus on development aid priorities in which the United Nations System has competitive advantages and thus constituted a very valuable input in the preparation of the UNDAF document. The CCA was finalized during the second half of 2005. The Country Team devoted itself to the preparation of the UNDAF throughout 2005 and during the first quarter of 2006. Throughout 2005 and early 2006, the heads of agencies discussed the progress and evolution of the UNDAF in United Nations Country Team meetings, making contributions and suggestions, and taking strategic decisions.
A second workshop was held towards the end of 2005, with representatives, heads and officials from all the agencies, funds and programmes of the United Nations System in Uruguay. This workshop had the support of system colleagues, in particular, of two members of the United Nations Staff College. It was possible to establish, by means of a participatory process, the results expected in each of the three assistance areas with their corresponding national priorities.
Lastly, two meetings were held in February 2006. In the first, all the System agencies were informed of the progress made throughout 2005; the second was devoted to adjusting and enriching the final version of the UNDAF. 
This final version of the UNDAF was presented to the national authorities and endorsed by them in March 2006.
The evolution of the results of the country programmes and the UNDAF outcomes will be monitored continuously by means of the quantitative and qualitative indicators established for this purpose (see “Monitoring and Evaluation Framework”). Additionally, evaluations will be held in the middle and at the end of the period, carried out by inter-agency teams which will also include government officials and monitoring and evaluation experts (see “Monitoring and Evaluation” section). 
As this is the first formal approach to the United Nations System’s harmonized programming in the country, the UNDAF process may be refined and revised annually on the basis of the ad hoc incorporation of new activities which the agencies may consider pertinent to deal with jointly; the development of new alliances, and, possibly, due to radical changes in national priorities. 
II.   Results
The process of defining the assistance areas for development took into account the following conditions:
That they should be a priority for the country.
That they should be a priority for the United Nations Country Team.
That the United Nations System in Uruguay should have comparative advantages in the assistance area in question. 
The assistance areas defined by the Country Team are included in the national priorities outlined by the government in its electoral proposals, as well as in the Strategic Plan embodied in the National Budget. 
The intervention of the United Nations System in Uruguay in support of the Uruguayan State, together with the efforts of the several actors involved, will help to achieve the results foreseen. It may be noted that in all the results expected, in the three assistance areas, two or more agencies of the United Nations System intervene jointly. This highlights how important the Country Team considers the increasing use which is made of the specific capabilities of the agencies and the synergy of joint work in the attainment of these results. 
Assistance Area 1:
Sustained and sustainable growth of the Uruguayan economy, with emphasis on the diversification of production, insertion in international markets (both within and outside the region), the increasing incorporation of scientific and technological innovation in productive processes and the growth of investment. 
The sustained and sustainable growth of the Uruguayan economy is a key area to support and encourage, always from a perspective based on human development. 
Uruguay’s economic, technological and scientific indicators show a situation in which a great many development opportunities unfold; therefore, it is relevant to devote efforts to the consolidation of strategic development, based on scientific investigation, innovation and the diversification of production. 
The following expected outcome within the Development Cooperation Framework has been identified (UNDAF Outcome): 
UNDAF Outcome 1.
By 2010, the country will have made progress in the generation of the capacity to incorporate knowledge, innovation and diversification of production of goods and services aimed at sustained and sustainable growth. 
The Country Programmes’ expected outcome, related to the UNDAF 1 Outcome, seeks to contribute to the sustainability of the process of growth in Uruguay. 
Assistance Area 2:
To reduce the significant levels of poverty which Uruguayan society has reached in recent years (in particular amongst the younger generations), with emphasis on the eradication of extreme poverty and the reduction of inequities (economic, social, inter-generational, gender, territorial and ethnic) in starting conditions and access to quality social services. 
The problems of poverty and inequities in starting conditions are at the centre of government concern in Uruguay. The inherent rights of the human being are not fulfilled if there is a lack of the capacity needed to take advantage of available opportunities for development as a productive, social, political and cultural being, from the perspective of rights, equality of gender and social integration. As regards the fight against poverty and the achievement of equity, it is worth noting the high priority assigned to the coordination and articulation of social policies carried out by the Uruguayan State. 
The United Nations Country Team has spelt out the following results to be expected from the UNDAF with regard to the second area of assistance:
UNDAF Outcome 2.1.
By 2010, the country will have advanced in the design and management of policies to eradicate indigence and reduce poverty. 
UNDAF Outcome 2.2.
By 2010, the country will have advanced in the design and management of policies which will make possible more equitable starting conditions and increased access to good social services as well as confronting discrimination and promoting processes of social integration. 
It is evident that both results focus on public policies capable of eliminating indigence and diminishing poverty and, simultaneously, of contributing to avoiding discrimination of all kinds and generating processes of social integration. 
Assistance Area 3:
To promote the exercise of all Human Rights and strengthen the quality of democracy, by increasing civil, political and social awareness. 
The third area is linked to the democratic institutions, the Uruguayan State and the need to consolidate and strengthen these institutions. All political and social actors in Uruguay today feel that it is necessary to extend human rights, in line with an integrated approach. 
It is evident from the statements of all the Uruguayan political parties that the consolidation of democratic governance is a priority and a goal in the country today. 
The cooperation of the United Nations System seeks to strengthen institutions in general and the State in particular. A solid institutional context and a reliable public administration are the best contribution to the fulfilment of the goals set by the country with regard to the MDGs.
The United Nations Country Team has identified the following result needed in order to attain the goals described above: 
UNDAF Outcome 3.
By 2010, the country will have advanced in the adjustment of national legislation and practices to its international commitments, and in the strengthening of public and civil institutions for the design, execution, monitoring and evaluation of public policies. 
As can be seen, this outcome seeks to harmonize national legislation with international regulations and to improve the processes of devising, implementing and monitoring national policies. 
UNDAF Results Matrix    
The results matrix presented in the enclosed document explains the links between national priorities, the UNDAF results and the Country Programmes. For each result or outcome, the matrix illustrates how the UNDAF guides the design of agency supported programmes and projects for the country. The matrix also shows how the main results of the agency programmes lead to the achievement of shared UNDAF outcomes, which go further than individual actions. It may be noted, too, that the results of the Country Programmes are shared by several agencies. The matrix identifies the agencies’ partners for each of the individual or shared outcomes, as well as the resource mobilization goals. 
The Country Programme Outputs column shows the specific outputs or services resulting from agency development actions. In every case, these outputs or services are related to technical assistance activities. The technical assistance or support activities provided by the agencies incorporate the perspectives of rights, gender and local development in a transversal manner. Thus, these three perspectives constitute integrating pillars in the design, implementation and evaluation of assistance, in the processes involved in carrying out this assistance and in the results expected. 
Human rights and the gender approach are included in all of the 100 Country Programme Outputs in the UNDAF matrix for Uruguay, although it may be noted that the two first outcomes of the Country Programme, in the two final UNDAF outcomes, focus explicitly on those rights (with 15 Country Programme outputs in all). While local development is present in 20 of those results, the goal is a resource mobilization of US$ 14,340,000 which represents 43% of the total resources established as a goal to be mobilized. 
III.     Estimate of Resource Requirements 
IV.   Execution
In order to attain each of the UNDAF outcomes, joint and coordinated action of the agencies of the United Nations System is foreseen. The matrix shows that all of the agencies of the United Nations System in Uruguay are involved.  
As regards the level of decision making, the coordination of action will be conducted by specialized groups of Representatives and experts, as well as by regular meetings of Representatives organized by the Resident Coordinator. 
In certain specific cases it is foreseen that during the period 2007-2010 the coordination of some interventions will also call for joint action and agreements regarding the allocation and outlay of resources.
V.    Monitoring and Evaluation
The Monitoring and Evaluation Plan
El monitoring of the outputs and outcomes of the Country Programme will be carried out by means of the following mechanism: 
Country Programme Outputs
Agencies will design their own monitoring indicators, which will be duly communicated to the Resident Coordinator’s Office. Likewise, individual agencies will be responsible for compiling information about these indicators, which will be sent to the Resident Coordinator’s Office for systematization within the framework of the UNDAF. 
Country Programme Outcomes
Taking as their base the established Monitoring and Evaluation plan, the designated agencies will be responsible for compiling and verifying the relevant information. In view of the fact that the Country Programme’s outcomes will be shared by various agencies, the specific monitoring roles of each of the agencies involved and the coordinated monitoring action—which may include joint visits to selected geographical areas, regular meetings of experts and Representatives, amongst other matters—will be jointly decided during the second semester of 2006 and will be organized by the Resident Coordinator’s Office. Similarly, as with the monitoring of outputs, the Resident Coordinator’s Office will be in charge of the systematization of information. 
The Country Programme Outputs monitoring process tends to be continuous, due to the nature of the agencies’ interventions. Compiling information for the monitoring of indicators, however, depends in many cases on the timely availability of information from the official sources of verification. In relation to this, it is suggested that specific monitoring activities be carried out twice a year and should coincide with the production of national statistics (regional, local sectorial, etc.).
The UNDAF 2007-2010 evaluation will be carried out in two stages:
A mid-term evaluation, during the fourth quarter of the second year of the UNDAF programme cycle (2008).
An end-of-term evaluation, during the fourth quarter of the final year of the UNDAF programme cycle (2010). 
The evaluation will be carried out by an evaluation team composed by:
A Resident Coordinator’s Office employee.
Two United Nations System employees (at least one of whom will belong to Agencies with harmonized cycles), preferably with experience in monitoring and evaluation.
A monitoring and evaluation expert from the Uruguayan Budget and Planning Department (abbreviation in Spanish: OPP).
The input for these evaluations will be (i) the information contained within the Monitoring and Evaluation framework, (ii) the records of the various monitoring processes, and (iii) meetings of consultation carried out by the different parties involved—essentially, government, international financial institutions and donors. 
The results of the mid-term evaluation will enable the necessary adjustments to be made to the UNDAF. Furthermore, the results obtained from the end-of-term evaluation will serve, in addition to its natural objective, as important input for the design and later implementation of the UNDAF for the following period.
